record.context_brief: Aztec diamond with a knight-move pair of deleted squares
record.original_question: Count the domino tilings of an Aztec diamond after deleting two close-to-central squares that are related by a knight's move and are as central as possible subject to that constraint.

evidence.quote: The two squares removed are a knight’s-move apart, and subject to that constraint, they are as close to being in the middle as they can be. Up to symmetries of the square, there is only one way of doing this.
Problem 8: Count the domino tilings of an Aztec diamond from which two close-to-central squares, related by a knight’s move, have been deleted.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, the Aztec diamond $AD_n$ is the union of all closed unit lattice squares whose centers $(x+\tfrac12, y+\tfrac12)$ satisfy $|x+\tfrac12|+|y+\tfrac12|\le n$. A domino is a $1\times 2$ or $2\times 1$ rectangle made of two unit squares; a domino tiling of a region is a covering of the region by non-overlapping dominoes. Two unit squares are said to be a knight's move apart if the displacement between their centers is $(\pm 1,\pm 2)$ or $(\pm 2,\pm 1)$.

Consider an Aztec diamond $AD_n$ from which two unit squares have been removed, subject to the following conditions:
(i) the two removed squares are a knight's move apart;
(ii) among all such pairs, the chosen pair is as close to the center of $AD_n$ as possible (up to the symmetries of the square, there is essentially only one such choice).

Find a closed-form expression (or product formula) for the number of domino tilings of the resulting region as a function of $n$.
